headline: BLM Backcountry Exploration and Primitive Camping Awareness
reservation: This region is managed by the BLM and does not require an entry permit for general sightseeing. However, specific activities like overnight stays in Goblin Valley State Park or group permits for certain canyons require separate arrangements. Always check the official BLM Price Field Office site for the most current dispersed camping and wilderness area regulations.

days.title: Canyon Rims and Ancient Art

stops.name: The Wedge Overlook
stops.detail: Gaze across the 'Little Grand Canyon' where the San Rafael River has carved a deep, multi-layered gorge through the limestone.

stops.name: Buckhorn Wash Pictograph Panel
stops.detail: Observe the haunting, life-sized red figures of the Barrier Canyon Style, an exceptional example of prehistoric rock art.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours for gravel road travel; conditions vary by recent weather.
days.note: Stay on designated routes to protect the fragile biological soil crusts.

days.title: Sandstone Slots and Hoodoos

stops.name: Little Wild Horse Canyon
stops.detail: Navigate a quintessential Utah slot canyon featuring narrow sandstone walls and natural light displays.

stops.name: Goblin Valley State Park
stops.detail: Walk among thousands of mushroom-shaped hoodoos in a geological playground.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for regional transfers; watch for washboarding on dirt access roads.
days.note: Slot canyons pose extreme flash flood risks; check regional weather before entering.

days.title: The Silent Heart of Sinbad

stops.name: Lone Warrior Pictograph
stops.detail: Locate this solitary and striking figure etched onto a desert varnish-covered wall in the remote Sinbad area.

stops.name: San Rafael Reef
stops.detail: View the dramatic 'cockscomb' of tilted rock layers that forms the eastern edge of the Swell.

days.driving: Allow 4 hours for backcountry navigation; high-clearance 4WD is often necessary.
days.note: Total isolation is likely; ensure your vehicle carries a full-sized spare and extra water.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Little Wild Horse Canyon is the most popular trailhead and can reach capacity during spring break. Arrive early or have a secondary hike planned in the nearby Temple Mountain area.

intel.title: Connectivity Limits
intel.text: Cellular service is virtually non-existent once you leave I-70 or the main highways. Download all maps for offline use before departing Green River or Price.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: There are no gas stations or services within the Swell interior. Top off your tank in Green River or Castle Dale and carry a gallon of water per person.

intel.title: Seasonal Heat
intel.text: Summer temperatures regularly exceed 100°F, making midday hiking dangerous. Plan strenuous activities for the shoulder seasons of April or October.

intel.title: Road Durability
intel.text: Backcountry routes like Buckhorn Draw can become impassable for standard vehicles after heavy rain. Verify road status with the BLM office during monsoon season.

plan.arrival: Pick up a high-clearance rental in Moab (CNY) and stock up on groceries and emergency supplies in Green River before entering the Swell.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance 4WD is strongly recommended for Sinbad and technical canyon access; check rental contracts for unpaved road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The Wedge Overlook offers panoramic western views, though shadow depth in the canyon varies significantly by month.
